It's interesting you mentioned a movie possibly not translating well and it makes me want to recommend The Castle to you. It's a very Australian film and I have long suspected it wouldn't translate well. It's sort of the Aussie equivalent of the Starsky and Hutch theme, not in terms of plot or style, but because S&H is so very, very American. The Castle is an iconic film here and it's very wholesome. The trick, I think, is not overthinking it.

"He didn't do a lot wrong except for not counting his drops (who does?)."

This is the man who told Danny, in his office, "I've sentenced boys younger than you to the gas chamber. Didn't want to do it...felt I...owed it to them." (Another line we quote all the time in my house, btw.) So he's not really a good person, either. He's not really the villain (although his trying to bribe Danny to throw the game in exchange for a scholarship is also pretty slimy), he's more the antagonist. Some of the humor comes in watching a pompous windbag get knocked down a few pegs, yes, and one of the things that is so great about Ted Knight's performance is that you feel for him even as you want to see him get his comeuppance, but the movie isn't suggesting he's evil, just that he's a douchebag. The humor is just in the clash between "Snobs vs. Slobs," not in anyone being a villain, per se. Mr. Mantooth and I, in discussing this right now, are realizing that Smails/Knight is actually the funniest character, with the funniest line delivery, in the movie.

(The joke with the lightning is because the man is a Bishop, and before being struck he yells that "The Good Lord would never interrupt the greatest game of my life!" That's why lightning is such a good payoff: God has literally struck him down/interrupted his game. Later in the movie we see him again, all disheveled and half-drunk, and someone refers to him as, "Reverend," and he snarls, "I'm just a man. My name's Fred. There is no God." Also, Murray leaving him there on the ground in the rain and speeding away is funny.)

Bill Murray has never been the funniest part of the movie; it's more the reactions of other people to him that are the funny part, though he has a few good bits. Like when Chevy Chase is talking to him (when he plays through in the night) and Murray is asking about his pool (implying he could come swim in it), and Chase's reply is, "We have a pool--we have a pond. Pond would be good for you." It's not Murray's joke, it's Chase's. The only real laugh line I ever thought Murray had was "We can kill the gophers, we don't even have to have a reason!" (along with its adjunct/previous line, "If we kill all the golfers, they're going to lock us up and throw away the key." The humor there is that he actually thinks he is being asked to kill all the golfers, at a golf course where he is employed, and that his only objection is that he doesn't want to go to prison). Oh, and his eating the candy bar in the pool that everyone thought was poop. I know some people do really think Murray is hilarious in that movie, but I found and still find his stuff the weakest parts of the movie. For me & my family (at least) the humor is the number of quotable/humorous lines just thrown out there:

"That's good luck." "...in Haiti."

"'What's that sign say?' 'No bare feet,'" and "Pick up that blood."

"Now I know why tigers eat their young."

"I bet if you buy a hat like that, it comes with a free bowl of soup. Oh...looks good on you, though."

"Well, the world needs ditch-diggers, too," [another of Judge Smail's classics, in response to Danny's inexpert fishing for college money/telling the Judge that he got into college but his parents can't afford it], followed by the other caddy's, "You know, I've often thought of becoming a golf ball."

Everything Smail's nephew says, because his voice and delivery are so smarmy and insufferable: "I want a hamburger...no, a cheeseburger. I want French Fries, I want potato chips..." (interrupted by Smails's, "You'll get nothing and like it!") and "It's the best, I got it from a Nee-grow." Oh, and when he drinks the whiskey with a cigarette butt in it and pukes in someone's car, and the owners get in the car without realizing it--gross, but amusing.

"I bet you were something when Ike was President. Want to make $14 the hard way?"

"Don't sell yourself short, Judge. You're a tremendous slouch."

The whole "Nnnnooonan! Missit! Missit! Noonan!" bit isn't really funny as-is but is funny when quoted elsewhere, as is, "I ain't paying no 50 cents for no Coke/Then you ain't getting no Coke." (And then Danny has to leave the cage and face the music.)

"Be the ball." "You're not being the ball, Danny." "Well, it's kind of hard with you talking like that." (And then, "Okay...I'm not talking...not talking...") And, "You take drugs, Danny?" "Every day." "Good." (And then, "Thank you very little.")

Smails's, "Welll? We're waiting!"--again, it's not the line that's funny in itself, it's Knight's perfect delivery. It's not surprising that you liked Smails--everyone likes him even as we laugh at him and dislike him--because, again, Ted Knight is so perfectly funny, every line, every scene. ("Gambling is illegal at Bushwood, sir, and I never slice." slices, throws club in fury and the old Billy Baroo.)

As for Danny's girlfriend and her terrible accent...I dunno. The terrible accent is fun, for us. In any given month in my house you're likely to hear, at least once, a terrible, "OH, DAT'S AHLL OI NEAHD!" in response to some inconvenience or situation. I mean, her name is "Maggie O'Hooligan." She's ridiculous, and her character/storyline is really just in there to put more pressure on Danny.

I dunno. Like I said, I think maybe it's a combination of some of it not translating well, and it seems like you were just expecting something very different--it's not really a clever comedy so much as a silly movie with a lot of humorous asides and throwaway lines. It's ridiculous and goofy rather than sharply hilarious, if you know what I mean. And it does get funnier on repeated viewings as you pick up the subtle bits, catch the throwaway lines, and know what to expect/get into the spirit of it more. But, you know, not everything is funny to everyone, either. I really expected, given how funny your comments/posts are, that the laugh lines in Caddyshack would be right up your alley...I'm sorry.

I really do recommend the others I listed, too, though, and really, really hope you like Galaxy Quest--we saw it in the theater and everyone laughed a lot and loved it, and our girls loved it, too, when they saw it, so hopefully you will, too, especially if you like Trek--you'll pick up on a lot of the little things, then. Sam Rockwell and Tony Shalhoub are especially funny in it, though of course everyone is funny in it. I could quote that one all day, too, though I won't since you haven't seen it. So even if you don't have to be locked down--yay, you! And I'm sure you did make a difference, even if it was as part of a group!--I still recommend you check them out. We regularly do movie-watchings in our house, where I make popcorn and we all sit together and watch something, so next time you're in the mood for a movie I hope you find something on my list you'd like, I really do. I always feel really bad when I recommend a movie to someone and they end up not enjoying it, so I feel like I have to make it up to you by you seeing another one I recommended and enjoying it (none of the others are like Caddyshack, btw).

I will definitely check out The Castle, thank you!
